appraisal_events.evidence: 'bien qu'il fût plus instruit, plus intelligent et meilleur que bien d'autres, il semblait impossible d'éprouver auprès de lui... autre chose qu'un spleen presque intolérable'; his falsely detached, self-concealing requests for invitations produce 'malaise, répulsion'; 'ce visiteur... ne fut presque jamais Saniette... je laissais venir, à la place, des gens qui étaient loin de le valoir.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Despite being more intelligent and worthy than many others, Saniette's anxious, self-concealing manner of angling for invitations repels rather than attracts sympathy, and the narrator repeatedly passes him over for lesser company.

appraisal_events.evidence: Albertine 'le regardait avec des yeux agrandis'; the waiter and Albertine 'avaient l'air d'être dans un tête-à-tête mystérieux... et dont j'étais le tiers gênant'; 'je sentis qu'on peut être près de la personne qu'on aime et cependant ne pas l'avoir avec soi.'
appraisal_events.explanation: At Rivebelle the narrator's sense of possessing Albertine's attention briefly collapses when she seems absorbed in a silent private rapport with a waiter, leaving him emotionally sidelined, though the passage notes he soon puts the impression behind him.

appraisal_events.evidence: 'je trouve ce genre de milieux cléricaux exaspérants... Ce sont des milieux où on fait tribu, où on fait congrégation et chapelle... on n'a pas assez de dédain pour les gens qui n'en sont pas... Tu en es, mon oncle Charlus en est.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup dismisses the Verdurin salon as a clannish, self-important sect, though the narrator notes this is borrowed, fashionable jargon, mildly undercutting Saint-Loup's own critical authority even as he scores the point.

appraisal_events.evidence: 'Comme tu dépenses de l'argent!'... 'Tâche de ne pas devenir comme Charles de Sévigné, dont sa mère disait: Sa main est un creuset où l'argent se fond'... 'je crois que tu es vraiment assez sorti avec Albertine... même pour elle cela peut sembler ridicule.'
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's mother gently but pointedly rebukes his extravagant spending and excessive time with Albertine, comparing him to a notorious spendthrift and warning that his conduct may look ridiculous.

status_effects.explanation: Saniette visibly craves invitations but disguises the craving out of fear of imposing, leaving him suffering and dependent while receiving nothing.
He is concretely, repeatedly passed over as a guest in favor of people who do not equal him, a witnessed and stated pattern of exclusion.
The narrator feels excluded and anxious when Albertine's attention seems to slip toward the waiter, though the passage frames this as a passing episode.
Albertine holds the emotional initiative in this moment, her attention seemingly elsewhere while the narrator is left anxious and dependent.
Her salon is characterized by Saint-Loup as a clannish, sect-like circle, a local discrediting reported within the dialogue.
The narrator's aside that Saint-Loup is merely adopting fashionable jargon slightly undercuts his own credibility even as he delivers his critique.
His mother's rebuke about his spending and his devotion to Albertine casts his current conduct as excessive and potentially ridiculous.

ambiguities: Saint-Loup's dismissal of the Verdurin salon is narrator-endorsed in substance but simultaneously undercut by the narrator's note that Saint-Loup is echoing fashionable jargon, so his own rhetorical standing is only mildly, not clearly, diminished.
